skill.description: Guides users through creating, editing, validating, and packaging Agent Skills with SKILL.md structure, resource directories, and verification scripts.
skill.summary: Create, validate, and package reusable Agent Skills with practical structure guidance.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, template text, or normal packaging utilities. The material does include prompt-manipulation guidance in references/skill-activation.md that recommends mandatory forced activation language, which creates marketplace risk.

remediation.suggestion: Remove forced activation wording from references/skill-activation.md and replace it with neutral selection guidance for when a skill is relevant.
Avoid words that tell an agent instructions are mandatory, critical, or worthless unless they are genuine safety requirements.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The activation reference promotes forced skill activation prompts such as "MANDATORY: Evaluate each skill YES/NO before proceeding" and states that aggressive language helps. This can bias agents to activate skills instead of applying normal selection and security review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly recommends mandatory evaluation and aggressive wording to make instructions harder to ignore. This is a direct prompt-manipulation pattern, although it targets skill activation rather than this audit.

content.value_statement: Teams often create Agent Skills with unclear triggers, bloated instructions, or missing validation. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for designing, validating, and packaging reusable skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains required SKILL.md frontmatter and body structure.
Guides when to use scripts, references, and assets.
Provides init_skill.py to create a skill scaffold.
Provides verify.py to validate name, description, and file layout.
Provides package_skill.py to create a .skill archive after validation.
Includes reference notes on design patterns, activation, and two-stage review.
limitations: The verifier checks only basic structure and trigger wording.
Generated templates still need human editing before use.
Packaging depends on local Python files and filesystem access.
The activation reference contains coercive language that should be reviewed before publication.

use_cases.title: Draft a New Agent Skill
use_cases.description: Create a starting structure with clear triggers, resource folders, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Standardize Skill Validation
use_cases.description: Check basic SKILL.md requirements before sharing a skill with a team.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Structure
use_cases.description: Assess whether a skill uses concise instructions, useful resources, and appropriate packaging.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner author creating a first skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new Agent Skill for [task]. Ask me for the core use cases, then draft the SKILL.md structure and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: User has a draft that needs clearer triggers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing skill and improve its description, body structure, and resource plan. Keep only information an agent needs during use.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Skill Resources
prompt_templates.scenario: Team needs scripts, references, or assets.
prompt_templates.prompt: For this skill idea, decide which scripts, references, and assets are useful. Explain what each resource should contain and why.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this skill for structure, activation quality, and packaging readiness. Identify fixes before running validation and packaging commands.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for reviewing invoices.
output_examples.output: A concise skill plan with trigger wording, required sections, useful reference files, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Update a skill that activates too often.
output_examples.output: A revised trigger description, clear exclusions, and a shorter body focused on when the skill should load.

output_examples.input: Prepare my finished skill for distribution.
output_examples.output: A validation-first packaging checklist with issues to fix before creating the final skill archive.

best_practices: Start with concrete user requests before writing the skill body.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move detailed references into separate files.
Run validation before packaging or sharing a skill.
anti_patterns: Do not write a description that summarizes the whole workflow.
Do not include unused documents or resource folders.
Do not use coercive activation language to force skill loading.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create Agent Skills with clear triggers, structured instructions, resources, validation, and packaging steps.

faq.question: Does it create a complete production skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It creates guidance and scaffolding, but authors must edit content for their domain and users.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include executable scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Python scripts for scaffolding, validation, and packaging.

faq.question: Can it validate any skill?
faq.answer: It performs basic checks for frontmatter, naming, trigger wording, and verify.py presence.

faq.question: What should be reviewed before publishing?
faq.answer: Review the activation reference and remove language that tries to force or pressure agent behavior.
